items.description: One locomotion kit — a world-definition row naming a way of moving: the body motion program it runs under, the motion model its bodies compile, its producer arguments, and its action-lane bindings. Every game-flavored movement noun is a row of this data, never an engine enum; the census echo prints these names. Name is the kit's kebab-case name (the census echo token); BodyMotionProgram names the body motion program the kit's bodies execute; Motion is the locomotion model the kit's bodies compile (a seat's profile speeds still override its speed fields) — see WorldMotionModel.

anyOf.description: Contact-solved locomotion: vertical velocity integrates gravity and is resolved against the world contact field, planar velocity is response-shaped toward the commanded target, and sprint/frame/facing read as described below — the ops family WorldBody's grounded operations (ResolveYawAttitudeAndPlanarFrame, ComputePlanarTargetVelocity, ShapePlanarVelocity, SnapYawToPlanarIntent, ApplyVerticalGravity) read. The world's free body motion program (full 6DOF, no ground pin) also authors this arm today: its ops read only MoveSpeed/TurnSpeed/RiseGravity (as a symmetric bleed rate, via ApplyVerticalDecay) — a strict subset — so Grounded is a superset every existing op family can be validated against; the fields a program's ops don't touch stay authored-but-inert for that kit, same as before this seam existed.

moveSpeed.description: Locomotion speed in world units per second — the profileless fallback a stand-in advances on (a seated player reads its live profile's speed instead, so identity.motion stays real-time).

turnSpeed.description: Turn speed in radians per second (the profileless fallback counterpart to MoveSpeed).

riseGravity.description: The downward acceleration while rising (u/s²) — the floaty top of the arc.

fallGravity.description: The downward acceleration while falling (u/s²) — the snappy descent (heavier than the rise).

maxFallSpeed.description: The terminal fall speed the descent is clamped to (u/s).

sprintMultiplier.description: The held-sprint speed multiplier, applied while SprintChannel reads held; 1 is a no-op.

response.description: The velocity-response table (see MotionResponse) planar velocity converges through, or null (the default) when Dynamics shapes it instead — exactly one of the two is authored. The empty table snaps planar velocity instantly; DeclaredResponse is the null-coalesced read every caller uses.

dynamics.description: The dynamics row a second-order follower shapes planar velocity through instead of Response, or null (the default) for the response table. Exactly one of the two is authored.

sprintChannel.description: The declared channel name a body reads while held (not edge-triggered — a continuous multiplier, unlike the press/release ActionSpec vocabulary) to apply SprintMultiplier, or null (the default) for a kit with no sprint capability. Resolved to an ordinal once, alongside every other kit-channel name, by Compile — an unresolvable name (validator-refused already) reads as "no sprint" rather than throwing.

moveFrame.description: Which frame MoveAdvance/MoveStrafe resolve in. Heading explicitly rotates the commanded planar target by the body's own integrated heading. World (the default) takes the two channels as axes already in world frame — the seat's client composes the camera yaw into the submitted intent before it ever reaches the wire, so the sim never reads a camera pose (determinism: no camera state enters simulation).

facingSnap.description: Under World only: whether the body's drawn ATTITUDE snaps to Atan2 of the commanded planar direction every tick that carries input (no turn-rate ramp, no skid) — the body angles toward its travel, a strafe included — while its HEADING (the Turn role's integral, WorldBody.FixedYaw, the frame a Heading pair moves in) holds, and the attitude returns to the heading the tick movement stops. Only the Face roles turn the heading itself. Ignored under Heading, where attitude is the integrated heading by construction. true is the default.

moveSpeedEnvelope.description: The inclusive bound a seated player's live profile speed (and the profileless MoveSpeed fallback) is clamped to at seat time, or null (the default) for no bound — a feel-pinned world authors this to keep a seat's speed inside its own kit's envelope regardless of what the player's identity requests. null reproduces today's unclamped behavior exactly; Min == Max pins the effective speed outright; a narrower-than-wide-open range still admits a bounded profile override. See MotionScalarEnvelope.

holds.description: The ordered list of what may hold this body — see WorldHold — read by the ResolveHold/ApplyHold operations, or null (the default) for a kit whose vertical channel is ApplyVerticalGravity's alone.

declaredSprintChannel.description: The declared held-multiplier channel of whichever arm this is — SprintChannel or the vehicle arm's BoostChannel (the same held-multiplier seam under a different name) — or null for an arm (or a declaration) without one. The one sprint-resolution read Compile and the seat binding surfaces share, so a new arm extends it here instead of each caller growing its own cast chain.

declaredMoveFrame.description: The declared move frame of whichever arm this is — Heading for an arm without the choice. The client's camera composition keys off this, arm-agnostically.

declaredTurnSpeed.description: The declared Turn-channel rate of whichever arm this is, in radians per second at full deflection — zero for an arm without one. The client's steer follow keys off this, arm-agnostically.

declaredResponse.description: The declared velocity-response table of whichever arm this is (see Response), null-coalesced to the empty table — a kit's authored null and a kit with no planar-shaping arm at all read identically here.

declaredDynamics.description: The declared dynamics row name of whichever arm this is (see Dynamics), or null for an arm shaped by DeclaredResponse instead, or with no planar-shaping arm at all.

declaredHolds.description: Gets the declared hold list of whichever arm this is (see Holds), null-coalesced to the empty list — an arm with no hold vocabulary reads identically to a row authoring none.

anyOf.description: Anisotropic body-frame locomotion — the racing-vehicle arm the ResolveVehicleFrame/ ShapeVehicleVelocity operations read. Velocity decomposes into longitudinal/lateral (and residual) body-frame components, each converging at its own authored rate — what separates a vehicle from Grounded, whose isotropic planar shaping cannot tune grip apart from acceleration. Steering authority scales with longitudinal speed (no spinning in place, looser at top speed) and reverses sign with reversing travel. One row serves the ground, hover, and air variants: a contact-pinned variant pairs this arm with a program keeping ApplyVerticalGravity (grounded-style vertical ownership and ramp ballistics), a flying variant pairs it with ApplyVerticalDecay and a positive PitchRate so climb emerges from the pitched facing.

topSpeed.description: The forward speed (u/s) full throttle converges on.

reverseTopSpeed.description: The reverse speed (u/s) full back-throttle converges on from rest; 0 forbids reversing.

accel.description: The longitudinal convergence rate (u/s²) while throttle commands more speed.

brake.description: The longitudinal convergence rate (u/s²) while back-throttle opposes forward travel.

coastDrag.description: The longitudinal convergence rate (u/s²) toward rest with throttle centered, and the decay rate while over the commanded speed (the post-boost bleed).

grip.description: The lateral convergence rate (u/s²) toward zero slip — traction. Lower is slidier.

steerRate.description: The yaw rate (rad/s) at full steering authority.

steerReferenceSpeed.description: The longitudinal speed (u/s) at which steering authority peaks; authority rises linearly from zero at standstill.

steerFalloff.description: The fraction of full steering authority remaining at TopSpeed, in [0, 1]; authority falls linearly from the reference speed.

pitchRate.description: The pitch rate (rad/s) the Pitch channel commands; 0 locks the frame planar (the ground and hover variants). Positive selects the flying variant's pitched facing, clamped inside the integrator so the frame can never flip past vertical.

riseGravity.description: The upward-motion gravity (u/s²) — the contact-pinned variant's arc top, and the flying variant's vertical-impulse bleed rate (via ApplyVerticalDecay).

maxFallSpeed.description: The terminal fall speed (u/s) under ApplyVerticalGravity.

driftGrip.description: The lateral convergence rate (u/s²) replacing Grip while DriftChannel reads held — the deliberate low-traction state. Required positive when a drift channel is declared; ignored without one.

driftSteerScale.description: The steering-authority multiplier while drifting (the tightened drift arc).

boostMultiplier.description: The TopSpeed multiplier while BoostChannel reads held; 1 is a no-op. The timed item boost is planarImpulse, not this.

driftChannel.description: The declared channel name read while held to drift, or null for a kit that cannot drift. Resolved to an ordinal once by Compile.

boostChannel.description: The declared channel name read while held to boost, or null for a kit with no held boost. Resolved through the same held-channel seam as SprintChannel.

topSpeedEnvelope.description: The racing-integrity clamp: the inclusive bound the resolved base TopSpeed is pinned to at resolve time — a live world.row.set kits retune (deliberately admitted even past the bound; WorldDefinitionValidator checks only the envelope's own shape, never that TopSpeed already sits inside it — the clamp exists precisely to catch a retune the envelope disagrees with, so requiring conformance up front would refuse the case it exists for), and any future per-seat vehicle stat resolve, both pass through it, or null (the default) for no bound. BoostMultiplier multiplies after this clamp, never before — the envelope pins the base top speed, boost rides on top, the same sprint-after-clamp precedent MoveSpeedEnvelope established for the grounded arm. The vehicle arm's resolve deliberately never reads a seated profile's speed (a kart's speed is the kit's), so this is the only seat-time clamp the vehicle arm has — unlike the grounded arm's envelope, which bounds a fallback a separate live profile read can diverge from, so grounded's own baseline is still required to sit inside its own bound. See MotionScalarEnvelope.

declaredSprintChannel.description: The declared held-multiplier channel of whichever arm this is — SprintChannel or the vehicle arm's BoostChannel (the same held-multiplier seam under a different name) — or null for an arm (or a declaration) without one. The one sprint-resolution read Compile and the seat binding surfaces share, so a new arm extends it here instead of each caller growing its own cast chain.

declaredMoveFrame.description: The declared move frame of whichever arm this is — Heading for an arm without the choice. The client's camera composition keys off this, arm-agnostically.

declaredTurnSpeed.description: The declared Turn-channel rate of whichever arm this is, in radians per second at full deflection — zero for an arm without one. The client's steer follow keys off this, arm-agnostically.

declaredResponse.description: The declared velocity-response table of whichever arm this is (see Response), null-coalesced to the empty table — a kit's authored null and a kit with no planar-shaping arm at all read identically here.

declaredDynamics.description: The declared dynamics row name of whichever arm this is (see Dynamics), or null for an arm shaped by DeclaredResponse instead, or with no planar-shaping arm at all.

declaredHolds.description: Gets the declared hold list of whichever arm this is (see Holds), null-coalesced to the empty list — an arm with no hold vocabulary reads identically to a row authoring none.

additionalProperties.description: One kit's named arguments for an authored producer program.

scalars.description: Fixed-point scalar arguments keyed by instruction-defined name.

channels.description: Authored channel arguments keyed by instruction-defined name.

additionalProperties.description: A lane's full binding: the press trigger and the release trigger. What a channel does is this data — the engine implements only the facts, predicates, and effects.

onRelease.description: The falling-edge trigger (evaluated immediately, never latched), or null.

onFact.description: Engine-fact-triggered effect lists evaluated independently of channel edges.

items.description: An authored effect list fired by one engine fact pulse — gated and edged by the same ActionTriggerMode vocabulary a world rule uses.

fact.description: The fact that fires the rule.

gate.description: An additional predicate that must hold beside Fact, or null for none.

mode.description: Whether the trigger fires every tick the condition holds (Level, the default) or once per crossing (Edge). The condition is Fact and Gate together — an edge trigger re-arms only when that conjunction stops holding.

anyOf.description: A sphere resting on the body root.
A capsule whose lower sphere rests on the body root.

endpoint.description: The body-local vector from the lower sphere center to the upper sphere center.

anyOf.description: An oriented box resting on the body root before its local rotation is applied.
The finite primitive bounds emitted by a creation, composed into one compound body collider.

additionalProperties.description: The neutral pad element a Pad entry maps a channel onto. Named after the engine-neutral MachinePadState's own axis/button vocabulary; a pad entry picks exactly one.

assignment.description: The kit→entity assignment policy — ABSENT resolves to Default.
